Engelsen! Tie them back to back and throw them in the sea, I say!
The Japanese captain
You shall not die. I have said it.
A sailor of the sloop
Wind's backing, sir. I don't like the look of those two sail to windward.
The sloop's boatswain
Fourteen of us, sir, and three of them Indians. Say the word.
The King of Laputa
(He is deep in a problem. A page strikes his mouth with a flap; he starts, as if waking.)
(He points to a book, then to the sky, and pronounces the words slowly.)
Stand quite still. Your altitude first, by the quadrant.
Sit, sit. Tell me of England: its laws, its customs. No one here will listen to me.
Mind the stone. Not one finger on it: it is poised so exactly that a child could turn it.
Ninety-three comets, and every period settled. The next will come in one-and-thirty years.
Welcome to the Academy! Five hundred rooms, and a projector in every one.
Give no offence, I beg you: they take it very hard here.
The Governor of Glubbdubdrib
I shall put everything into their tongue, sir, and theirs into yours.
A person of quality
Have you seen any of our struldbrugs, sir, our immortals?
The King of Luggnagg
(The King returns some answer you cannot understand; your interpreter bows.)
Captain Theodorus Vangrult
A surgeon, eh? Half the usual rate, then, if you'll physic my men.
(He gently flaps his master's ear with the bladder.) Pardon, sir: he will attend to you directly.

The Hollanders' ship sails soon, they say.
Good fish this morning, from beyond the islands.
Mind your step on the stones.
Have you come from very far?
Only the Hollanders may trade here.
A fisherman of Xamoschi
A ship from the east? Rare, rare.
Papers, if you please.
A guard of the palace
The Emperor gives audience today.
You have letters from the King of Luggnagg? Then you are expected.

🌌 The Astronomer's Cave. A hundred yards down, under its dome, the twenty lamps burning, and the great loadstone in the middle.
The door of a Laputian house
An angler on the gallery
(He does not look round.) The fish below are very large this season. I calculate it by the arc of the line.
A Laputian gentleman
A lady of the court
(He stares upward, and says nothing, until his flapper touches his mouth.) Ah. Have you considered the conic sections?
The comet, sir. Have you heard? In one-and-thirty years it will come again.
(Humming a scale.) Pardon. The music of the spheres is especially fine this morning.
Triangles, rhomboids, cycloids: everything has its figure.
I have asked the King's licence to go down to Lagado. Twice. He was thinking.
A gentleman on the gallery
A lady watching the anglers
The land is very far down today.
We may go lower when the King pleases.
The door, out to the island
The master of the house
The lady of the house
(He is drawing circles on a slate and does not see you. His flapper coughs.) Ah! A visitor. Do you know any music?
Oh, a stranger! Sit, sit. My husband has not spoken to me since Tuesday: he is working out the orbit of a comet.
A lady taking the air
The clouds are below us today. One forgets they are clouds.
My husband has not looked down in eleven years. He says there is nothing there that cannot be calculated.
They bite best when the island passes over the sea.
A stargazer at the rail
The comet is due in thirty-one years. We have checked the sum four hundred times.
Look: the sun is a little smaller than yesterday. I am almost sure of it.
Down there they plough with hogs. Up here we plough with numbers.
A lady of the town
A tailor with his quadrant
(He walks with his eyes on the sky until his flapper taps his shoulder at the corner.) Ah. The street turns. Thank you, Bliffmarklub.
Every street here runs true to the compass, sir. The houses, I grant you, do not.
(Humming.) The fourth note of the scale is off today. Can you not hear it?
My husband is at his figures. He has been at his figures since Michaelmas.
The tailor measured me with a quadrant and a pair of compasses. The coat came six days later and fits nobody.
Mutton in triangles, beef in rhomboides! Fresh this morning!
MUTTON · BEEF · PUDDING, CUT TRUE
INSTRUMENTS · MATHEMATICAL & MUSICAL
A musician of the square
(He tunes a string, very carefully, to a star.) The music of the spheres, sir. We play it every evening, so the court need not stop thinking.

The stone is level: the island stands still.
Attracting end down, and we sink; repelling end down, and we rise. A child could do it, if it knew which end was which.
The sun is going out, sir. Slowly. Very slowly. But surely.

New method. Can't stop. The Academy says it will double the crop in a year, or ten.
Dig, and fill, and dig again. They say it improves the soil.
No corn this year, nor grass. But next year!

A man of Lagado at home

Sit, if you can find a stool that stands. My husband pulled the old ones apart: the Academy has a new way to make chairs.
We tore down the old house and built it again by the new rules. It leaks, but the rules are excellent.
A projector's clerk
A builder of the new method
Can't stop! The scheme! The scheme!
My house? Pulled down. The new method will build it better, when it is finished.
Spare a farthing for a projector, sir? For the encouragement of ingenuity?
The Academy will make us all rich. In a few years.
Look at that roof. Built from the top down. Like the bees.
The door, out to the Academy street
A student of the Academy
A projector with a petition
My project wants only a little money, sir, for the encouragement of ingenuity.
I have a scheme for making the sea flat. Calm, I mean. Permanently.
I was once a man of business. Now I am a man of projects!
The projector of sunbeams
Eight years, sir, eight years upon this project: to extract sunbeams out of cucumbers, put them in phials hermetically sealed, and let them out to warm the air in raw inclement summers.
The oldest student of the Academy
The calciner of ice
Gunpowder, sir, from ice, by calcining it. I have also written a treatise on the malleability of fire, which I intend to publish.
The ingenious architect
A new method of building houses, by beginning at the roof and working downward to the foundation. The two prudent insects, the bee and the spider, do the same.
(He is blind from his birth, and so are his apprentices.) I mix colours for painters, by feeling and smelling. A little mistaken now and then. But the professor himself is generally mistaken also.
A blind apprentice
This one smells of red. I think.
The projector of hog-ploughing

Bury acorns, dates, chestnuts in an acre of ground, six inches apart, eight deep: drive in six hundred hogs, and in a few days they root it all up and dung it besides. Saves ploughs and cattle and labour!
The projector of spiders
Why employ silkworms, when we have such plenty of domestic insects who could both spin and weave? Feed them flies of the right colours, and they spin it already dyed.
An astronomer of the Academy

I am putting a sundial upon the great weathercock of the town-house, adjusting the annual and diurnal motions of the earth and sun, so as to answer and coincide with all accidental turnings of the wind.
I cure colics by contrary operations, with a large pair of bellows, sir. Mostly. The dog is quite well, I assure you.
The softener of marble
I am softening marble, sir, for pillows and pincushions. It takes a long while. Feel this one. No, it is not soft yet.
The breeder of sheep
I hope to propagate the breed of naked sheep throughout the kingdom. Two, so far. Rather cold, poor things.
The professor of the Engine

By my contrivance the most ignorant person, at a reasonable charge, and with a little bodily labour, may write books in philosophy, poetry, politics, law, mathematics, and theology, without the least assistance from genius or study.
A pupil at the Engine
(Turning a handle.) Thirty-six turns a day, sir. Six hours.
A sage with his pack
(He opens his pack, takes out a hat, a spoon and a little bird, and shows them to you one after another, in silence. Then he waits for your answer.)
Another sage with his pack
(He sets down a candlestick and a plum. You understand he is asking whether you have dined.)
The professor of mathematics

Each proposition and demonstration is written on a thin wafer, with ink composed of a cephalic tincture. The student swallows it upon a fasting stomach, and for three days eats nothing but bread and water.
The professor of politics

Our professors propose schemes for persuading monarchs to choose favourites for their wisdom, capacity and virtue. They are all quite mad, of course. And now we come to the matter of discovering plots...
Another projector of politics
I have a very good scheme: tax every man by the vote of his neighbours for his own good qualities. Wit, valour and politeness. He will pay gladly!
One of Lord Munodi's tenants
My lord farms the old way. Our neighbours laugh at us, and they are hungry.
Good grapes this year, as every year.
The projectors call us ignorant. Well, we eat.
A servant of Lord Munodi
Lady Munodi's waiting-woman
My lord will see you in the hall.
Everything here is done as it was done in my grandfather's day. My lord likes it so.
The door of the old mill
The door, out to the river
She's ground the corn of this valley a hundred years, and she'll grind it a hundred more, if they let her be.
THE NEW MILL (UNFINISHED)

No ship for Luggnagg this month, friend. Not one.
Glubbdubdrib? Five leagues south-west. The island of sorcerers. You'll see things there.
A room? Upstairs, the second door.
A sea-captain at home
Luggnagg lies to the south-east. A month's wait for the trade wind.
Welcome! We are sea folk here, not projectors, thank heaven.
A sailor of Maldonada
Fair wind for Glubbdubdrib today.
Fresh fish! None of your Academy fish, either.
Mind the bales, sir.
Luggnagg? Next month.
